newsitem.title: FRANCE: Negotiations resume in French truck strike.
newsitem.headline: Negotiations resume in French truck strike.

text.p: Talks between drivers and French haulage bosses resumed in Paris on Monday evening to try to break the deadlock in a hardening eight-day truckers' strike.
Negotiators said talks had resumed at around 1630 GMT in the presence of a state-appointed mediator.

Conservative Prime Minister Alain Juppe renewed an appeal to truckers and haulage companies to reach a deal in talks over the strike slowly squeezing the French economy and provoking friction with France's neighbours.

"I'm following the talks hour by hour," Juppe said after a marathon all-night round of talks between bosses and drivers ended in deadlock over strikers' demands for higher wages, shorter hours and retirement at age 55 rather than 60.
